Necromancer · Hybrid

Blood Wave Necromancer - Self-Found Variant

one-button blood caster, Mythic-free

Necromancer hybrid unchanged one-button blood caster, Mythic-free based on Blood Wave Necromancer

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 14

Move on whenKessime's Legacy equipped. Everything else on this page is optional; that is not.
Move on whenBanished Lord's Talisman on the amulet and the three greater-affix Lucky Hit restore tempers landed on your jewelry. In the base build this stage ends when you craft Ring of Starless Skies; here the tempers are the substitute and they are strictly worse, which is the point of the variant.
Move on whenComfortable at Torment 4 with the 25% Resource Cost Reduction floor held and Aspect of Redirected Force ready to go on the block-chance rebuild.

Skill bar

1Reap
2Blood Wave
3Blood Lance
4Sever
5Bone Prison
6Blood Mist

Rotation

Unchanged from the base build: Sever onto a pack, which drops a corpse; Blood Mist eats it for Flesh Eater and teleports you again; Blood Lance from range to dump Overpower, then hold Blood Wave to regain it; Bone Prison on anything that survives; weave Reap when Essence runs dry. Expect to weave Reap far more often than the base guide implies - that is what not owning the ring feels like.

Skill point priority

  1. Same Starter shell as the base build: this is an endgame guide and its own author defers 1-70 to Maxroll's separate levelling guides, so this stage is a level-70 Torment-1 entry point rather than a levelling route
  2. Blood Wave to max first, and take Hematolagnia the moment it is available - it is the key passive that makes Blood Wave a Core skill with no cooldown, and the build does not exist without it
  3. Blood Lance next, purely as the Overpower-stack spender that re-triggers Bloodbath
  4. Bone Prison for the attack speed the guide leans on hard
  5. Sever, Blood Mist and Reap at one point each
  6. Variant note: chase Essence Regeneration on every slot that can roll it before you chase damage. With no Mythic ring coming, resource is the thing that will stop you, not damage

1Reap

4Sever
5Bone Prison
6Blood Mist

Rotation

The loop runs itself from here: the Wat rune applies Decrepify, Life Tap generates Blood Orbs, and the Teb rune spends them on Iron Maiden for Vulnerable. Rotate Sever and Blood Mist for movement and otherwise hold Blood Wave, with Bone Prison on anything tanky.

Skill point priority

  1. Blood Wave and Hematolagnia maxed - unchanged, everything else is support
  2. Bone Prison maxed: the attack-speed engine
  3. Blood Lance kept only for the Bloodbath and Overpower-spend loop
  4. Sever and Blood Mist stay at one point
  5. Stat gates for this stage, taken from the base guide: over 15 Essence Regeneration, over 25% Resource Cost Reduction, three greater-affix 'Lucky Hit: Chance to Restore Resource' tempers on jewelry, over 60% Critical Strike Chance
  6. Variant note: the base guide relaxes the 25% Resource Cost Reduction gate at the next stage because Ring of Starless Skies arrives. Here it does not, so treat 25% as the permanent floor

Skill bar

1Reap
2Blood Wave
3Blood Lance
4Sever
5Bone Prison
6Blood Mist

Rotation

Identical to the early endgame. What changes is the gear, not the gameplay - and here that means one aspect swap, not two: Disobedience onto the boots and nothing onto the bug.

Skill point priority

  1. Blood Wave and Hematolagnia maxed; Bone Prison maxed for the attack-speed cap
  2. Blood Lance held at the rank that keeps the Overpower loop turning
  3. Stat gates: over 15 Essence Regeneration, over 25% Resource Cost Reduction (not the base build's relaxed 15% - that number assumes the Mythic ring), over 70% Critical Strike Chance, over 50% attack speed
  4. Survivability is the open problem and this variant answers it with Aspect of Disobedience rather than the base build's Embattled Aspect plus Endurant Faith, because that package leans on instant fortify healing the guide itself calls a bug

Rotation

Read the base guide's warning first, because it kills characters: Decrepify is how Resolve stacks are generated, and you start a Pit run with none. Open on a small pull, cast Blood Wave until Resolve is around 10, then push. Steady state: Blood Lance from range before every pack, Bone Prison before contact, Corpse Tendrils for Vulnerable and Flesh Eater, Blood Mist every eight seconds, Blood Wave held down. Without Blood-Mad Idol, packs take longer and you have more room to make a mistake in - play to that.

Skill point priority

  1. Sever comes off the bar for Corpse Tendrils with the Jaws Of Death variant: it makes the cast instant and consumes corpses, which activates the Flesh Eater paragon node for a 60% damage multiplier
  2. Bone Prison on cooldown - attack speed and physical cover
  3. Blood Lance now does double duty: Overpower spending and triggering Aspect of Disobedience for damage reduction
  4. Hard gate, unchanged from the base build: 100% block chance, which is what activates Aspect of Redirected Force
  5. Variant note: with no Blood-Mad Idol the push ceiling is lower and the character is meaningfully harder to kill. That is the trade this whole file makes

How to run them

The base build's own guide hires Aldkin while gearing, for the 15% Critical Strike Chance and the early sustain, and switches to Subo from the midgame for map visibility and a 25% Critical Damage multiplier. That switch is a bet that crit chance has been solved by gear, and without Mythics it has not been, so this variant simply never makes it. The Reinforcement is unchanged and is the part every source agrees on: Raheir on Bastion, whose picks are inherited from the base build unchanged. The hire's picks are not inherited and could not be: the base build's planner payload records Subo's tree, not Aldkin's, and no source publishes an Aldkin allocation for a Necromancer. So the two recorded above are the two that can be stated without inventing anything - his Perk, which is granted to every hire rather than chosen, and the one Aldkin skill the knowledge base names anywhere. Treat the rest of his tree as open, and read the base build's page for the Subo allocation if you take the midgame switch after all.

Plan

Said plainly: this is an activity-level allocation, not a per-build one. No guide for this build publishes War Plan picks - the Season 14 planner payload behind the base build carries no War Plans data at all, and every War Plans guide in existence organises its advice per activity rather than per build. So the picks below are Maxroll's build-agnostic endgame progression priorities, tagged with the activity that owns each node, and they are the same nine any Season 14 character would take first. No `level` is recorded because no source publishes an order: the feed carries no per-node level and a planner stores a plan as an unordered set.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.

  • Writhe and Rot

    Hellwyrms will always spew Maggots that gain +1 Monster Power. Sometimes, a Pang of Duriel will also crawl forth. Lair Keys often burst out of Pangs of Duriel.

    Maxroll's endgame-progression page puts this first across every build it discusses: Hellwyrm experience plus lair keys.

  • Hellmouth

    When a Hellwyrm emerges, it unleashes one of the following: A Chaos Rift, which releases varied rewards upon collapse. Maggots, which burst out Experience Orbs when slain. Bloodseekers, which are more likely to drop Ancestral items when slain.

    More Helltide density, which is where the keys come from.

The Undercity2 of 11 nodes chosen

100%

  • Node
  • Activity root
  • Jade Epiphany

    When you gain an Attunement level in the Undercity, Experience Orbs appear around you. All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

    Undercity is the fastest targeted-slot farm in the game and this build wants specific slots.

  • Gutter Filth

    When you activate any Beacon within the Undercity, there is a small chance to summon a Portal Prankster. Invasion Portals will sometimes summon Rats of varying amounts.

    Same run, more of it.

100%

  • Grigoire's Gambit

    After opening a Tortured Gift in Helltides, there is a chance Grigoire's knights will ambush you. When killed in Helltide, they may drop Unique Items available from his Hoard Chest.

    The second priority on the same page; lair bosses are where this build's uniques live.

  • Two by Two

    After opening a Hoard Chest, there is a low chance a Portal will open that will take you to the Nemesis Lair, where you will fight two Initiate Lair Bosses at the same time. Slaying both will yield great rewards. You cannot enter a Nemesis Lair from Belial's throne room.

    Doubles up lair boss encounters, which is a straight multiplier on unique acquisition.

    Begin The Pit carrying the Heart of Stone, a fragile relic that is dropped after taking sustained damage and breaks after dropping 10 times. While you carry it, enemies can drop bonus Progress Orbs. After slaying the Guardian, Choron's Pedestal appears. Deposit the Heart of Stone within to gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance.

    Pit is where glyph levels come from and this build gates on glyph level.

  • Choron's Blessing

    Gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance for completing The Pit.

    Second Pit node on the same reasoning.

Uniques & where to find them

Kessime's Legacypants

The build's enabler and the only item here that is not optional - it fires two waves per cast and pulls monsters into them. Gamble pants at the vendor, and target-farm Andariel (Hanged Man's Hall, east of Tarsarak, Kehjistan; 1x Greater Lair Key, keys from Initiate lair bosses). The plain Unique is fine; this variant never upgrades it.

Where →
Banished Lord's Talismanamulet

General Unique Pool, so any lair boss can drop it - which is exactly why it is the one special amulet this variant chases: it needs no Horadric Cube conversion and no Mythic. Run whichever Initiate lair boss you already have keys for.

Where →
Ring of Starless Skiesring 1

Mythic Unique. Rare drop from any lair boss, or a Horadric Cube craft with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic can be equipped at a time. It is listed because the gear model this variant inherits equips it at the last two stages, not because the variant needs it: every stat gate on this page is the base guide's pre-ring number.

Loot filter

maxroll.gg
Blood Wave Necromancer - Maxroll Light / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes)

Same three in-guide import codes the base build uses, because the affix pool is the same one. Use the Light tier rather than Strict here: this variant deliberately never crafts a Mythic, so it needs to keep seeing the Legendary jewelry and the Essence-regeneration rolls a Strict endgame filter hides. Preview the code before importing.

Summary

The same Blood Wave loop as the class's meta build, re-cut for a character that will never hold a Mythic and does not want to lean on a bug. Two things drive every change here. First, the base build's progression is written around crafting Ring of Starless Skies: it is what drops the Resource Cost Reduction requirement from over 25% to over 15%, and until it lands the build is resource-starved. In Season 14's Solo Self-Found mode there is no trading to shortcut that, so this variant is written to be playable without the ring: Essence Regeneration and Resource Cost Reduction stay at the front of every jewelry priority for the whole run and the base guide's pre-ring 25% Resource Cost Reduction gate is treated as permanent. The ring is still drawn on the late-endgame and push rows because the gear model here is the base build's own planner payload and that payload equips it; the difference is that no advice on this page leans on it. Second, the base build's endgame survivability package is Embattled Aspect plus Endurant Faith, and its own guide says in writing that the instant fortify healing this relies on 'is a bug'. That is the single most nerf-exposed thing in the Season 14 build set, so it comes out and Aspect of Disobedience takes the slot - less effective, and it will still be there after the next hotfix. The trade is honest: this is a slower, squishier, more resource-gated Blood Wave that survives a patch. Play the meta build instead if you have the Mythics.

Reasoning

Based onBlood Wave Necromancer
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. The progression stops assuming Ring of Starless Skies. It is still shown on the late-endgame and push rows, because this variant inherits the base build's planner payload for its gear model and that payload equips it - saying otherwise would misdescribe the page. What changes is that nothing below depends on it: the base guide relaxes its Resource Cost Reduction gate from over 25% to over 15% the moment the ring lands, and this variant holds 25% for the whole run so the character is playable without it. Treat the ring as a bonus, not a milestone.
  2. Essence Regeneration and Resource Cost Reduction lead the ring and amulet priorities at every stage, not just the early ones. The base build relaxes Resource Cost Reduction to over 15% once the Mythic ring lands; with no ring the guide's own earlier gate - over 25% - stays in force to the end.
  3. Embattled Aspect is dropped from the late-endgame boots and replaced with Aspect of Disobedience. The base guide states outright that 'Embattled Aspect makes your fortify healing instant (it is a bug)'. Disobedience's stacking armour is worse and is not a patch target.
  4. The push stage keeps Banished Lord's Talisman on the amulet instead of swapping to Blood-Mad Idol. Blood-Mad Idol is the base build's damage-over-survivability trade and it is also a Mythic; both reasons point the same way here.
  5. Aldkin is hired rather than Subo. Maxroll's own guide hires Aldkin 'especially during the early game' for the 15% Critical Strike Chance and switches to Subo from the midgame - a switch that assumes the crit chance has been solved by gear. Without Mythics it has not been, so the gearing-stage hire stays hired.
  6. Adds an explicit War Plans allocation, which the base build does not carry: its planner payload has no War Plans data. The picks are Maxroll's build-agnostic activity priorities and the war_plans summary says so.
